Reviews online average around 4.5 stars on (Apple, 2024), reviews are largely 
positive, however complain that the app is buggy. Students were typically 
satisfied with the level of detail and educational experience, however some 
complained that it was missing large topics such as the “Battle of Hastings”. 
The website loosely follows recommendations from the scientific literature and 
could be improved. (British Dyslexia Assosiation, 2022) estimates that at least 1 
in 10 people suffer from dyslexia. Students with dyslexia may struggle to learn 
from eLearning sights that require extensive reading. Bitesize attempts to 
remedy this with podcasts, however, a potentially better alternative would be to 
include a screen reader so that the student can also view images and go through 
the lesson as it was designed. 
The lesson reviewed by the author took around 15 minutes to complete, which is 
towards the upper limit of what is recommended by the literature; additionally, 
the lesson was rarely broken up with questions. These aspects would in theory 
reduce student engagement, performance, and satisfaction. 
2.5.2 Seneca 
Seneca is an online learning platform similar in style to Bitesize. Seneca that has 
videos, notes, and practice questions (Olivia, 2024). Seneca has a huge range of 
topics subjects and lessons for KS2, KS3, GCSE, and A-Level (Olivia, 2024).  
For the review the author completes a lessons from GCSE biology 1.1. The key 
findings are (1) each lesson took around 2 minutes to complete, (2) multiple 
questions were asked within each lesson, (3) Seneca kept a note of failed 
questions, (4) students could easily cheat when answering questions by looking 
at the lesson’s contents above the question.
